{{Commonscat|Ficus superba }}
'''''Ficus superba''''',<ref>Miquel FAW (1866) ''Ann. Mus. Bot. Lugduno-Batavi'' 2: 200.</ref> also known as '''sea fig''' or '''deciduous fig''', is a [[hemiepiphyte|hemiepiphytic]] tree of genus ''[[Ficus]]''. It is a tree native 
to Indochina (Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam), southern India, and parts of Malesia (Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, Sulawesi, and the Maluku Islands including [[Seram Island|Seram]]).<ref name = powo/>
It is one of the species known as [[banyan]]s or "strangler figs" because of its potential to grow as a [[hemi-epiphyte]] and eventually progress to the strangling habit of species in this subgenus. It is, however, not an obligate hemi-epiphyte and can be found growing as single stemmed trees in forests. According to [[E.J.H. Corner]], if this fig germinates in a boulder field its roots can extend "extraordinary distances, up to several hundred feet" over and between the rocks.<ref>{{cite book | last= Corner | first= E.J.H. | date= 1940 | title= Wayside Trees of Malaya | location= Kuala Lumpur | publisher= Malayan Nature Society | pages= 527 - 529}}</ref>

== Formerly recognized varieties ==
Several varieties are now recognized as synonyms of other species:
* ''F. superba'' var. ''alongensis'' {{small|(Gagnep.) Corner}} is a synonym of ''[[Ficus alongensis]]'' {{small|Gagnep.}}<ref>[http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2812492 The ''Plant List'' (retrieved 17 January 2020)]</ref>
*''Ficus superba'' var. ''henneana'' is a synonym of ''[[Ficus henneana]]'', native to northern and eastern Australia.<ref>{{cite POWO |id= 89127-3 |title= ''Ficus superba'' var. ''henneana'' (Miq.) Corner|access-date= 7 September 2026}}</ref>
* ''F. superba'' var. ''japonica'' {{small|Miq.}} is a synonym of ''[[Ficus subpisocarpa]]'' {{small|Gagnep.}}<ref>[http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2812494 The ''Plant List'' (retrieved 17 January 2020)]</ref>
